subject: Allocation of incident liability & order form redlines — security addendum linkage
messages:
From: Sam Riley <sriley@acmedata.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@acmedata.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form — allocation of incident exposure

Jonas,

Thanks for the call this morning. We reviewed the draft Order Form and the security addendum you sent. Our legal team is pushing back on how incident-related liability is carved into the MSA and want a clearer sub-limit tied to a quantitative figure rather than an undefined allocation. Key asks from Acme: 

- A discrete sub-limit for data-security incidents (separate from general liability cap). They prefer a stand-alone number that is not a percentage of the order value.
- Explicit carve-outs: regulatory fines and third-party claims should be carved out from the sub-limit and handled via indemnity.
- Exclusion of consequential damages to remain, but we want express language that consequential cannot be recharacterized through other remedies.
- Tie the sub-limit to section 3 of your Security Addendum — we need the addendum to define the incident scope and remediation obligations precisely.

We can move fast on execution if we land numbers — otherwise this will be a blocker for procurement. Can you propose a compromise position and share redlines? I attached Acme’s preferred clause (PDF excerpt).

Thanks,
Sam Riley
Sr. Counsel, Acme DataWorks
---
Attachment: Acme_incident_clause_excerpt.pdf (pdf)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sam Riley <sriley@acmedata.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form — allocation of incident exposure

Sam — appreciate the clarity and the attached excerpt.

High level response: Redwood is open to a standalone numeric sub-limit for security incidents, but we need the sub-limit to be calibrated to the commercial commitment and to preserve carve-outs for third-party claims tied to our indemnities. We also want to ensure any carve-out does not create open-ended exposure for repeated incidents.

Proposed interim approach (for discussion):
- Two-tier incident waterfall: (1) First-party remediation and notification costs (to be uncapped up to a defined reasonable amount) paid by Redwood. (2) Separate monetary sub-limit for indemnifiable losses arising from a security incident capped at a numeric amount or the fees paid in the prior 12 months, whichever is greater/negotiated.
- Explicit carve-outs: regulatory fines remain indemnity-driven (we will ask for evidence & defense control carve-out language).
- Consequential damages: keep exclusion language; add anti-recharacterization sentence.

Looping in Laura (legal) and Neha (commercial) to shape precise redline language. Laura — can you draft a tracked-change suggestion that ties the Order Form figure to the Security Addendum section reference? Neha — heads up on potential pricing impact if we agree to a standalone sub-limit.

Best,
Jonas
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form — allocation of incident exposure

Jonas / Neha —

Thanks — I reviewed Acme’s language and drafted a clean compromise that balances our operational risk with their procurement needs. Key points in my redlines (attached as Acme_Security_Addendum_redlines.docx):

1) Numeric sub-limit: propose a fixed sub-limit of $2,000,000 for "Security Incident Liability" in the Order Form. To keep economics predictable, include optional upward adjustment tied to annual committed spend bands.

2) Defined scope in Security Addendum: insert a definition for "Security Incident" in section 1.1 of the Addendum that excludes incidents arising solely from customer-controlled misconfigurations and requires Customer to follow our published onboarding controls.

3) Carve-outs and indemnity linkage: carve out regulatory fines, statutory penalties and third-party claims from the Order Form cap; those remain subject to indemnity. Add cross-reference: "Notwithstanding Section X of the MSA, Security Incident Liability (as defined in the Security Addendum) shall not include regulatory fines, criminal penalties or third-party indemnifiable claims."

4) Consequential damages: preserve exclusion and add anti-recharacterization sentence: "For the avoidance of doubt, no recovery under any other remedy shall be construed as consequential damages."

5) Sunset and repeated incidents: limit the application of the sub-limit to losses arising from the same root cause within a 24-month rolling period to avoid perpetual stacking for unrelated events.

I attached the docx with tracked changes. Happy to walk through the new language with Acme. If they cannot accept $2M we can consider a tiered structure based on committed ARR — but that will require pricing adjustments.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Acme_Security_Addendum_redlines.docx (docx)
From: Sam Riley <sriley@acmedata.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@acmedata.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T14:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form — allocation of incident exposure

Laura / Jonas — thanks for the thoughtful proposal. A couple points from Acme’s side after internal review: 

- We can accept a numeric sub-limit but $2M is higher than Corpus can approve without board escalation. Our preference is $1,000,000.
- We still need regulatory fines to be explicitly carved out and handled via indemnity with defense control for Acme (we would accept cost-sharing mechanics only in narrow cases).
- The 24-month rolling period is acceptable, but we cannot accept a definition that shifts responsibility for onboarding misconfigurations to Acme unless Redwood provides more prescriptive operational evidence (checklists, onboarding runbook).

Can we land on $1M with the same carve-outs and an execution timeline: redlines to be finalized within 5 business days, then DocuSign signature. I have procurement availability the week of Dec 7. If you can provide a clean Order Form (PDF) with redlines accepted/unaccepted highlighted, we’ll route internally.

–Sam
Sr. Counsel, Acme DataWorks
